subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — autoscaling & throughput sizing
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@retailco.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Dedicated capacity — autoscaling & throughput sizing

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: generation for product descriptions + conversational search rerank. Average sequence length ~512 tokens, occasional long generations up to ~1k tokens.
- Peak concurrency: you mentioned bursts up to ~120 concurrent users; steady peak ~60–80.
- Availability target: 99.9%+; tolerable short tail latency spikes during burst windows if we have graceful fallbacks.
- Secondary workload: embeddings index + reranker pipeline used at query time (offline index, realtime rerank).

Key integration points we discussed:
- SDK setup & auth: support for API keys (hosted) and mTLS / customer-managed auth (Private) for Dedicated. SDKs include built-in retry/backoff and streaming support.
- Routing & model variants: requests can be routed by policy (latency vs cost). We can configure a primary high-quality model and a lower-cost fallback for burst traffic.
- Structured output / tool-calling: function-calling / JSON schema validation available for structured outputs. We can set up strict schema enforcement for the product description generation.
- Embeddings & rerankers: offline embedding index + lightweight reranker at query time is a common pattern. We recommend batching and async pipelines for embeddings ingestion.
- Autoscaling & sizing: Dedicated pools scale by adding GPU nodes; we support warm pools, soft/hard concurrency limits, and request queuing with priority routing.

Attachments: I’ve attached the workload sample you promised (retailco-workload-sample.json) — please also share any recent production traces or logs if available. I’m attaching a quick sizing proposal draft for the Dedicated pool (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
1) Share production sample logs + QPS/RPS traces (you).
2) Schedule a 60-minute architecture deep-dive with our Solutions Architect and infra lead (we suggested Tue/Wed next week).
3) We’ll circulate a sizing & cost estimate + example commit structure (reserved pool options).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate times once you confirm availability.

Best,

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our infra team after reviewing the sample: 

1) Peak concurrency: we typically see steady peaks around 60–75 concurrent generation requests; burst testing shows short windows up to ~120 concurrent. Is queuing + graceful fallback sufficient for the bursts, or do you recommend provisioning additional reserve GPUs?

2) Cold starts / warm pools: how long does a cold start for a generation model typically take in Dedicated? We’re sensitive to cold-start latency for low-traffic regions.

3) Prefix/KV cache behavior: for conversational flows we rely on KV cache. Does Redwood preserve cache across scaled replicas or will we see increased token latency during scaling events?

4) Throughput & GPU guidance: for a 1k token generation, can you provide rough tokens/sec and requests/sec estimates per GPU (A100 vs H100) so we can model costs?

5) Auth: we’ll be using a VPC Private Dedicated deployment. We’d like to use mTLS for node-to-control-plane auth. Does the SDK require additional config for mTLS?

If you can answer the above and include rough throughput numbers that’d be great — happy to schedule the deep-dive next week.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Engineering, RetailCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@retailco.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@retailco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — autoscaling & throughput sizing

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great questions — below are concrete answers and recommendations based on the workload you shared. I’ve kept this focused on Dedicated capacity architecture.

Autoscaling model:
- Node-based scaling: we add/remove GPU nodes from the dedicated pool. This is the primary model for predictable throughput.
- Warm pools: we maintain a configurable warm pool (x nodes) to reduce cold-starts. Warm nodes keep model artifacts loaded and KV caches primed.
- Soft/hard concurrency limits: per-tenant soft limits queue requests when concurrency is exceeded; hard limits reject. Queuing is preferred to avoid tail failures and we implement priority queues for critical routes.
- Burst queues: instantaneous bursts are handled by a prioritized queue; if queue time exceeds threshold, requests get routed to fallback model variants.

Cold-starts & cache behavior:
- Cold-start (load + JIT/compile) for a generation model on A100-80GB typically 12–30s depending on compilation (less with pre-warmed pools). H100 tends to be slightly faster for compile-heavy steps.
- KV/prefix cache: KV caches are tied to the serving process. When requests move to a new replica, cache is cold until warmed. We mitigate this with sticky routing for sessions and warm pools for critical traffic.

Throughput & sizing guidance (rule-of-thumb numbers):
- Generation (1k sequence length, medium complexity model):
  - A100-80GB: ~1,000–1,500 tokens/sec per GPU (sustained) depending on batch size and sequence length; ~6–10 concurrent streaming generation sessions per GPU at 1k tokens when using 32-bit or bf16 paths.
  - H100-80GB: ~1,500–2,200 tokens/sec per GPU under similar conditions; concurrency similar but better headroom for quantized pipelines.
- Embeddings: much higher throughput per GPU when batched (thousands of vectors/sec); embeddings workloads typically run on separate, denser pools or CPU+GPU hybrid nodes.

Concurrency & queuing strategy:
- Start with an initial pool sized for steady-state: if you expect steady peak ~75 concurrent streams at ~1k tokens, 4x A100 gives you ~24–40 concurrent sessions (depends on batching). We recommend starting with 4x A100 and a warm pool of 1–2 nodes, monitor, then scale to 8x if you need sustained concurrency >40.
- For predictable SLA-backed throughput, reserve capacity with a commit (Reserved Pool) and configure autoscale thresholds for burst-style scaling.

Routing & fallbacks:
- Configure primary route to high-quality model; fallback route to smaller/quantized model for burst windows. Route by latency or cost buckets.

SDK & auth:
- SDK supports API keys for hosted and mTLS for Private/Dedicated. For mTLS we provide cert rotation tooling; SDK requires adding the client cert/key to the transport layer — we have examples in our Private deployment docs.

Structured output & tool-calling:
- Function-calling (JSON schema) is supported. We can enforce strict schema validation and return structured confidence metadata. Great for product description generation where you have a rigid schema.

Embeddings + reranker pattern:
- Ingest embeddings offline (batch), store in your vector DB. At query time, retrieve top-K, then run a lightweight reranker (smaller model) in the Dedicated pool to reorder results. Keeps cost down while improving quality.

I’ve attached a draft sizing proposal (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf) with examples for 4x and 8x GPU pools and cost ranges. Happy to walk through line-by-line on the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Tom — happy to confirm and schedule. Quick ballpark numbers and next steps below (we’ll provide a more detailed cost worksheet before the deep-dive):

Ballpark throughput (1k token generation):
- A100-80GB: ~1,000–1,300 tokens/sec per GPU => ~1.0–1.3 requests/sec at 1k tokens (streaming generation); concurrency per GPU ~6–8 long-running streams.
- H100-80GB: ~1,400–2,000 tokens/sec per GPU => ~1.4–2.0 requests/sec at 1k tokens; concurrency per GPU ~8–12.

If you need sustained concurrency ~75 we recommend starting with 8x A100; 4x A100 + warm pool handles 40–50 concurrent streams with good queuing and fallback rules. Embeddings and rerank can be colocated but often run on separate optimized pools for cost efficiency.

Pricing/commit: yes — reserved Dedicated pools are available (monthly/annual commits). Reserved pools can include a guarantee for N warm nodes (configurable as part of the contract). I’ll have our finance rep produce a few pricing scenarios (4x A100, 8x A100, 4x H100) ahead of the deep-dive.

Next steps: 
- Please confirm preferred deep-dive time (we can do Tue 9 Mar 10am PT or Wed 10 Mar 11am PT).
- Share any additional production traces or SLO targets you want us to bake into the sizing.
- I’m attaching a one-page sizing summary (sizing-summary-quicklook.xlsx) and the draft proposal PDF.
- I’ll also open a HubSpot deal record and share a DocuSign SOW link prior to the call.

Proposed agenda for the 60-minute call:
1) Quick recap & objectives (5 min)
2) Walk through sizing & cost scenarios (15–20 min)
3) Deep-dive on autoscale, queues, and cache behavior (20 min)
4) Open items / next steps & timeline to commit (10–15 min)

If those times work I’ll send a calendar invite and include our infra lead.
